title: Authorizing shipment views, assignments, and carrier status updates
name: Shipment status routes

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these routes check whether the caller may read or change a shipment? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A dispatcher from org A calls GET /shipments/:id for a shipment created by org B. What is the response?
choices: 200 with the shipment, since dispatchers can see all shipments

questions.prompt: Two requests from the assigned carrier try to move the same in_transit shipment, one to out_for_delivery and one to exception, at the same moment. What happens?
choices: Both succeed and the last write wins
One succeeds; the other gets 409 concurrent_update because updateStatus is conditional on the version both requests read
The second request waits for a row lock and then applies on top of the first

questions.prompt: A carrier tries to move a shipment from created straight to in_transit. What happens?
choices: It succeeds, because in_transit is a valid carrier status
409 invalid_transition, because created has no carrier transitions
403 forbidden, because only dispatchers can update created shipments
400, because the request body is invalid
